stem: A Dayvigo prescription is three months old and has two completed refills. Which federal limits must the pharmacist check before the next refill?

choices.text: Check only whether five refills have been completed.
Check only whether six months have elapsed.
Check both the five-refill cap and the six-month issue-date deadline.
Require renewal now because two prior refills exhaust the limit.
Use a one-year window because Dayvigo is prescribed for sleep.

explanation.core_reasoning: Check both the five-refill cap and the six-month issue-date deadline. By contrast, 'Check only whether five refills have been completed.' uses a legal trigger absent from the stem.

choice_analysis.A: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Check only whether five refills have been completed.
choice_analysis.B: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Check only whether six months have elapsed.
choice_analysis.C: The stated facts support this result: Check both the five-refill cap and the six-month issue-date deadline.
choice_analysis.D: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Require renewal now because two prior refills exhaust the limit.
choice_analysis.E: This near-miss uses a different trigger: Use a one-year window because Dayvigo is prescribed for sleep.

related_facts: lemborexant (Dayvigo) is used for treatment of insomnia with sleep-onset or sleep-maintenance difficulty; it is federal Schedule IV and Massachusetts Schedule IV.
A Schedule III or IV prescription may not be filled or refilled more than six months after issue and may not be refilled more than five times unless renewed by the practitioner.
explanation.mpje_trap: Reject 'Check only whether five refills have been completed.' because its legal trigger is absent.

reasoning_steps: Classify lemborexant under the federal and Massachusetts schedules before selecting a legal pathway
Match the scenario's operative facts to Federal Schedule III and IV refill limits
